text:
nisha: FYI escalating FinTechX outage — their requests are showing up in us-east despite region=eu-west. They see 401 'invalid_audience' and p50 latency ~320ms. Repro steps from customer below.

james_customer: reproducer:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```
Response: 401 {"error":"invalid_audience","message":"audience mismatch: us-east"}
Headers seen by customer: X-Forwarded-For: 10.10.0.5, 34.200.12.9

nisha: Can you paste the full X-Redwood-Request-ID and the exact timestamps? I already see a billing spike attributed to our us-east prefixes.

kai: Quick read — likely SD-WAN partner doing internet-breakout and NATing the traffic to a US egress. If our auth is region-scoped, a request that physically arrives at us-east will fail audience validation. Can you capture a pcap/tcpdump on the peering egress while reproducing? e.g.
```
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 34.200.12.9 and port 443 -w /tmp/fintechx-egress.pcap
```
Also send over the X-Redwood-Request-Id from the failing response.

nisha: request-id=rr-20240405-abc123. Excerpted headers from their failing call:
```
X-Redwood-Request-ID: rr-20240405-abc123
X-Redwood-Region: eu-west
Host: api.redwood.ai
X-Forwarded-For: 10.10.0.5, 34.200.12.9
```

devon: Confirming hypothesis — auth expects a eu-west audience claim. When the packet egresses via the partner's US gateway it hits our us-east cluster and the token audience doesn't match, yielding 401. That also explains the latency and why billing shows us-east traffic. Short-term workaround: ask the customer to target eu-west.api.redwood.ai (regional endpoint) or provision a dedicated Private endpoint with a static egress IP. Long-term: partner needs to prefer eu-west for that customer prefix or advertise a eu-west NAT IP.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT INC-2024-345 created for cross-region egress causing auth failures and billing misattribution :rotating_light:

maria_billing: Noted — we'll flag the us-east usage and prepare to waive any surprise overages once routing is corrected. Need exact spike window (timestamps).

james_customer: traceroute from their appliance (shows partner exit to US):
```
 7  34.200.12.1  220 ms  210 ms  215 ms
 8  ae3.us-east-gw.partner.example.com  230 ms  231 ms  229 ms
```

kai: Action items: 1) nisha — upload pcap + full headers for rr-20240405-abc123; 2) devon — draft guidance for the SD-WAN partner (BGP communities / prefer-eu policy); 3) maria — hold billing adjustments. If partner won't change immediately, we can provision a dedicated endpoint and hand over a static egress IP to avoid NATing to US. We'll attempt a routing policy tweak tonight if partner allows.

nisha: Uploading pcap to secure share now and offering the dedicated endpoint option to FinTechX.

devon: I'll also add clearer auth-logging for audience mismatches so support can immediately surface region vs token errors.

nisha: Thanks team :thumbsup: will update once partner responds.
